_doc: THE MERGE QUEUE. The manager SCHEDULES merges; it does not resolve the
conflicts that not scheduling them causes.
⚠️ THIS FILE DID NOT EXIST UNTIL 2026-09-03, AND ITS ABSENCE IS THE POINT.
The day manager ran a merge queue that morning -- it declared an order, it
held sessions at position 2+, it promoted and poked -- and it worked. But it
existed only in that session's context. It was cited to a sub-session as
'the state of record ... created today', and a search of every branch and
every commit in the repo found NOTHING: not on main, not on any ref, not in
history. What existed was docs/runbooks/merge-queue.md, which is prose.
That is the exact failure the operator named on 2026-09-03: 'that's one of
the base functions of what a manager session is supposed to do. That needs
to be canonized. It's not something you take upon yourself in the session.'
A queue held in a session's head dies with that session, and the next
manager re-derives it from scratch -- or does not, and the morning repeats.
MEASURED HARM on the day the queue was invented, which is why it exists:
26 merges to main, 19 of them (73%) touching a shared register, five of
those the manager's own and two of THOSE bare lease heartbeats -- merges
whose entire content is a timestamp. Every one re-conflicted every open PR
touching a register. #10918 went dirty three times; #10923 the moment it
went green. Sessions burned ~16-minute pytest-runs that were void before
they finished.
THE INVARIANT THIS FILE EXISTS TO HOLD, and the one check_manager_scope.py
R8 enforces: AT MOST ONE ENTRY IS REBASING AT A TIME. Two sessions rebasing
against the same moving main is the thundering herd the queue prevents; it
is also the state that looks fine to each session individually, which is why
it needs a check rather than a convention.
PROMOTE AND POKE. A session does not poll. When position 1 lands, the
manager sets the next entry to `rebasing` AND messages that session. An
entry left `waiting` with nothing ahead of it is a session sitting idle for
a promotion nobody sent -- the 46-minute block the operator caught, in a
different costume.
STATES, NEVER COLLAPSED:
waiting   -- in the queue, not yet cleared to rebase. Do NOT rebase.
rebasing  -- cleared, and the ONLY entry that may be. At most one.
green     -- rebased, CI passed, waiting on the manager's merge click.
merged    -- landed. Keep the row until the next manager reads it.
blocked   -- cannot proceed; `blocked_on` says why. NOT `waiting`:
'not my turn' and 'cannot go' are different facts.
⚠️ `green` IS THE STATE THAT COST US. #10923 sat green and mergeable from
11:01:05Z to 11:11Z and the OPERATOR noticed before the mechanism did. The
manager's own 11:04Z sweep timer was enabled, carried next_run_at 11:04:00Z,
and never fired -- no error, no log. A cadence check that graded whether a
sweep was ARMED would have passed straight through that hole, because it WAS
armed. See check_manager_scope.py's R7 note for what is and is not covered.
note: ⚠️ THIS FILE WAS STALE FOR TWELVE HOURS AND THAT IS MY OWN FAILURE, RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY REPAIRED. It read 'queue EMPTY as of 2026-09-08T07:06Z' while I merged roughly nine PRs and ran an eleven-PR HOLD that existed only in my session context and in PR comments. That is MI-102 exactly — a queue run successfully for a day in one session's head, cited as 'the state of record', and found on no branch and in no commit — and a cold successor reading this file would have seen an empty queue and started merging the held PRs. R8 passed throughout, correctly: its one invariant is 'at most one entry rebasing', which an empty list satisfies trivially. A guard that cannot fail on emptiness is not evidence the queue is being kept. STATE 2026-09-08T18:58Z: eleven entries. #11391 is next and everything else is BLOCKED on the hold that protects it. RELEASE THE HOLD the moment #11391 lands, and say so on the PR. WHAT PASSED THROUGH MY QUEUE TODAY AND IS NOT LISTED HERE (the ledger this file should have been carrying): #11403, #11406, #11407, #11412, #11426, #11430, #11433, #11434, #11435 merged BY ME, and #11370, #11384, #11418 self-landed under my hold — twelve, every one verified present in origin/main's PR list rather than recalled. ⚠️ STATE THE POPULATION: main took 94 commits today across roughly 96 distinct PRs, so MOST of today's landings were not mine and this is not a ledger of main. It is a RECONSTRUCTION from my own session record checked against the log, not a contemporaneous record — which is the point. || CORRECTED 19:20Z, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE POINT. I wrote these nine automation rows as `blocked` on my own queue-hold. THAT WAS WRONG AND IT WAS A FALSE BLOCKER. Reading #11431's CI log rather than assuming: guards PASS 53 / FAIL 1 / SKIP 38, the one failure pr-landing-guard, cause R13 -- the branch arms auto-merge while its own committed session-board names somebody else's branch in merge_slot. Measured across all nine: every one arms, not one holds the slot. A bot writes no claim, so this NEVER self-heals and re-running CI is pointless. THE HOLD WAS RELEASED AT 19:00Z AND NOTHING MOVED, which is how I found out. ⚠️ I ALSO MIS-READ THIS ONCE MORE ON THE WAY: I grepped a local guard run for 'FAIL' and reported api-tier-policy as the failing guard. It was not -- that string is that guard's own PLANTED self-test defect, and its last line says 'self-test OK'. Grepping a log for a word and calling it a verdict is the unprovenanced-diagnostic trap this repo has a guard for, committed by the manager, twice in one pass. || THE CLASS IS ALREADY FILED AND I DID NOT FILE A FOURTH ROW. backlog_search returned BL-20260908-R13-MAKES-EVERY-AUTOMATION-PR-WRITE-THE-MERGE-SLOT-SO-MAIN-CAN-NEVER-BE-QUIET at 0.75 overlap (open), beside BL-20260908-R13-MAKES-EVERY-CONCURRENT-ARMED-BRANCH-WRITE-THE-SAME-SINGLE-MERGE-SLOT-SO-N-LANES-ALL-HOLD-IT-AT-ONCE and BL-20260908-R13-FORCES-EVERY-SELF-LANDING-BRANCH-TO-REWRITE-ONE-5-LINE-OBJECT-SO-CONCURRENT-PRS-CONFLICT-BY-CONSTRUCTION -- three rows on this guard already. What is NEW here is only the COUNT and the fact that it does not self-heal, and that belongs in the manager's own instrument rather than in a fourth row; this file is where a successor manager looks. Filing another would be the accumulation the repo already complains about. || ⚠️ AND THE GUARD CAUGHT ME DOING THE THING THIS FILE IS ABOUT. My first push wrote those two ids with an ELLIPSIS, copied from backlog_search's truncated output. artifact-validity-guard (scripts/ops/check_backlog_refs.py) failed the PR: 'this change introduces tracking reference(s) that resolve to NOTHING'. A row citing BL-X where BL-X was never filed reads as TRACKED while being tracked by nobody -- which is exactly the false-blocker class this entry was written to correct, committed inside the correction. Both ids are now the full ones, verified against docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json rather than retyped. MI-200's PR reported the identical finding on itself today ('four tracking ids I wrote with an ellipsis that resolved to nothing'), so this is a RECURRENCE of a same-day lesson, not a fresh one. || 19:29Z. QUEUE WORKED, and the R13 diagnosis is now PROVEN rather than argued: #11436 was red on guards 53/1, I changed NOTHING but the merge-slot claim, and it went 5 of 5 green and merged as 1b3b1d9b. So the blocker really is R13 and nothing else. SEVEN automation PRs remain in exactly that state and each needs the same hand-claim. SIX automation PRs remain, all on R13 and nothing else — the diagnosis is now proven THREE times (#11436, #11425, #11423: slot claim was the only change, guards went PASS 53/FAIL 1 -> green each time). ⚠️ AND NONE OF THEM IS URGENT, WHICH I HAD WRONG ONE TICK EARLIER. I called #11425/#11423 'the ones worth the slot' because they refresh clocks a guard reads — right about the mechanism, WRONG about the urgency: I had generalised check_digest_liveness's 6h window, and check_pr_queue_watch's is 30h while check_trainer_capture_watch's is 15h. Measured 19:32Z, all three FRESH (0.82h/6h, 14.3h/30h, 8.0h/15h). The remaining six are stale snapshots later runs supersede; work them for tidiness, not on a clock. ⚠️ AND CHECK EACH RECEIPT AGAINST MAIN'S BEFORE MERGING — an older one moves the clock BACKWARDS, which is why #11431 was CLOSED rather than merged. || ⚠️ 20:11Z — THE LINE ABOVE SAYS 'SIX AUTOMATION PRS REMAIN' AND THAT IS WRONG BY MORE THAN 4×. MEASURED at 20:03Z over the COMPLETE open-PR list (list_pull_requests state=open, 29 rows, not a sample): **26 of the 29 open PRs are automation**, every one on R13. The six I wrote were the six I happened to have touched — I recorded a snapshot of my own attention and called it the remaining set, which is the same unstated-population error this file already complains about, committed by me inside the instrument that exists to prevent it. The census is now in `entries` rather than in prose: reconcile-open-prs ×11, session-reaper ×4, error-feed-digest ×3, work-digest ×2, plus #11361 m7, #11366 probes, #11368 due-list, #11382 PR-queue receipt, #11386 m28 valuation, #11428 constraint readout. Non-automation open: #11337 (Tier-3, landing: hold — correctly waiting on the OPERATOR, not on me), #11347 and #11355. || ⚠️ AND IT IS A GENERATOR, NOT A PILE, WHICH IS THE PART THAT CHANGES WHAT A MANAGER SHOULD DO. Every merge to main spawns a reconcile-open-prs, and often a work-digest — INCLUDING MY OWN BARE LEASE HEARTBEATS. Five new automation PRs appeared in the 75 minutes after #11436 landed (#11438 #11439 #11442 #11444 #11445). At roughly 18 minutes per hand slot-claim cycle and at least one spawn per merge, draining them one at a time WHILE STILL MERGING NEVER CONVERGES — the queue is not a backlog to work down, it is a standing rate. That is exactly what BL-20260908-R13-MAKES-EVERY-AUTOMATION-PR-WRITE-THE-MERGE-SLOT-SO-MAIN-CAN-NEVER-BE-QUIET says in its own title, and I did not file a fourth row for it. ⚠️ THE CONSEQUENCE FOR A SUCCESSOR: do NOT open a session on 'drain the automation queue'. None of these is urgent (all three clocks measured FRESH at 19:32Z), each is a snapshot a later run supersedes, and CHECK EACH RECEIPT AGAINST MAIN'S BEFORE MERGING — an older one moves a clock BACKWARDS, which is why #11431 was CLOSED rather than merged. The fix is the guard, not the queue. || 20:36Z. THE QUEUE ANSWERED A SUB-SESSION THIS PASS, which is what it is for. #11450 landed MI-168's record correction and #11347/#11355 are closed as superseded. R13 is now proven on one variable FOUR times (#11436, #11425, #11423, #11450): the slot claim was the only change each time. ⚠️ THE 26 AUTOMATION ROWS BELOW ARE STILL NOT WORK — three more merges happened this pass and each will have spawned another. Read the 20:11Z entry above before touching them. ⚠️ AND NOTE WHAT THIS FILE STILL CANNOT SAY: two of the four rows above are recorded `merged` when they were CLOSED, because the state vocabulary has no `closed`. A successor reading the state alone would conclude #11347's content landed under its own number. It did not — it landed inside #11450.

digest_clearance._what: How to clear digest-liveness when it is about to go `stale` and red every open PR. THIS CORRECTS THE PROCEDURE I CARRIED IN MY OWN WAKES FOR THREE HOURS, which named the wrong artifact and would have wasted the pass it was written for.
digest_clearance.⚠️_the_stuck_receipt_prs_CANNOT_clear_it: THE CARRIED PLAN SAID 'land the newest stuck work-digest PR'. THAT IS WRONG AND WOULD HAVE CLEARED NOTHING. check_digest_liveness grades the receipt on the MERGED TREE, so landing a receipt OLDER than the one main already carries advances last_digest_age by zero. Read per branch at 04:16Z, generated_at: #11442 2026-09-08T19:23:13Z · #11445 19:54:09Z · #11452 20:35:07Z · #11465 22:42:40Z · #11471 23:49:25Z. EVERY ONE IS OLDER than main's 00:58:39Z. They are dead weight on the queue, not a clearance path. ⚠️ AND THERE ARE FIVE, NOT FOUR — #11471 was absent from my own carried list, so the count I was managing to was wrong as well as the method.
digest_clearance.the_only_proven_clearance: DISPATCH-THEN-ARM, and it is proven exactly once end to end. At 00:57:49Z I dispatched work-digest.yml (run 34297202160); it opened #11477 on automation/work-digest-34297202160-1; I pushed a merge_slot claim naming THAT branch onto it (42d9251f — check_manager_scope graded it 'a LANDING act, not an item' under the R2 carve-out); it merged 01:04:29Z. Verified AFTER, against a fresh main rather than inferred from the merge: `digest-liveness: OK state=fresh last_digest_age=0.38h`.
digest_clearance.⚠️_timing_matters_a_dispatch_can_produce: Run 34298416713 (event=schedule, 2026-09-09T01:14:57Z) completed `success` and opened NO PR, because digest_due correctly said not-due against the then-fresh receipt. So a dispatch fired early yields nothing to arm and is not a way to bank clearance in advance. Fire it CLOSE to the window — ~06:50Z for this one.
digest_clearance.⚠️_not_a_new_finding_do_not_re_file: work-digest.yml declares `20 * * * *` and had no run at all between 01:14:57Z and 04:16Z (3.0h).
